CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
February 3, 2021 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s  Executive  Order  N-29-20(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf), please note that
members of the public will only be allowed to observe and address
the Planning Commission Meeting of February 3, 2021 at 7:00 P.M. by
telephone, video and other electronic means, as follows:

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited
  video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/
   The above access options provide the public with the
  opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting.
   However, members of the public who wish to orally address the
  Planning Commission must use the public access options noted
  below:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 5120305##

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:

    When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
    If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an
  area with good reception.
    If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute
  the sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from
  the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making
  public comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members
of the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda,
comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on February 3, 2021,
the day of the meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting
date and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior
to close of the public hearing will be made part of the official
public record of the meeting.

Following Pages]

3.  Communications from staff.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 3, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, February 3, 2021 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting was called to
order at 7:05 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
  Chairman Larry Springs
Excused
Absence:  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECDD Director
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that Commissioner Trejo called earlier and has an
Excused Absence.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None, and the AT&T Operator verbally confirmed that there were no
participants on the line to speak.

5 to 7 minute Recess to resolve audio/visual synchronization.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-010 (SP-2020-010) 132 SOUTH MARKET
STREET: A public hearing to consider an application by Brion Moran,
representing The Dime for Special Use Permit No. 2020-010
(SP-2020-010) to allow 1) the on-site consumption of beer, wine, and
distilled spirits, 2) indoor live-entertainment; and 3) outdoor bar
area in an existing 3,500 square-foot two-story commercial building
on an approximately 4,625 square-foot H-C (Historic Core) zoned
property at 132 South Market Street.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick stated that she will reserve her questions for
the applicant.

Commissioner Rice asked for clarification regarding if there is still
going to be a user friendly component where customers will still be
able to order food from outside sources.

  1
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

- Mr. Salazar stated yes, the customers will be able to order their
  meals from outside sources.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated no questions for staff and will
address the applicant.

Chairman Springs asked for the applicant to come forward and address
the planning commission.

Brion Moran, Representing the Dime, along with Lucy Tredway and
Andrew Fiscella.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments to speak
for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST

None. This was affirmed by the AT&T On-line Operator.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-094, and adopt a resolution recommending City
Council adoption of SP-2020-010 and was seconded by Commissioner
Patrick, that Resolution No. 1892;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION OF
  THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  CERTAIN SPECIAL UNSE PERMIT FOR BRION MORAN
  (REPRESENTING THE DIME) TO ALLOW A BAR WITH 1)
  ON-SITE CONSUMPTION OF BEER, WINE AND DISTILLED
  SPIRITS, 2) INDOOR LIVE ENTERTAINMENT, AND 3)
  OUTDOOR BAR AREA IN AN EXISTING 3,500
  SQUARE-FOOT TWO-STORY COMMERCIAL BUILDING ON AN
  APPROXIMATELY 4,625 SQUARE-FOOT H-C (HISTORIC
  CORE) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT 132 SOUTH MARKET
  STREET.

Be approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, and Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained there is no appeals process.

5B. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001) CHAPTER 12 IMC:
A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2020-001
(ZCA-2020-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code to
modify regulations for off-hour parking for major event patrons and
tailgating, citywide.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick stated that she had no questions.

  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

Commissioner Rice stated to staff:
 This model does not work. True that the Arenas and Stadiums may
  need local parking for several of their events that will take place
  here in this city, and you are speaking of tying-up a minimum of
  6 to 8 hours of parking spaces which will include coming early to
  get the parking space, staying late to retrieve the parked vehicle,
  and a minimum charge of at least $25.00 per car at maybe a total
  of 10 parking spaces several of the community businesses will
  attempt to assist the arena/stadium meaning a possible $250.00 an
  event, but this business model does not work, just on the parking
  alone.

Commissioner Patrick stated she did have a question for staff:
 Tailgating parking usually occurs on Sundays, and to be located
  in the areas of the stadium seems alright, but in the Marketplace
  which is generally utilized by the public for shopping on those
  days, will there be a designated location set-aside for the
  tailgating/parking of those vehicles during game day where the
  public will not be put out of their parking space convenience?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated they would have to obtain a Special Use Permit,
  because the businesses would be open and operating at the same
  time, therefore they would have to demonstrate that they have
  the additional parking spaces available.

Chairman Springs asked Ms. Wilcox;
 For clarification that the businesses would have to obtain a
  Special Use Permit prior to hosting any form of Tailgating and that
  the proper amount of spaces must be available for them to utilize
  their place of business?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that in order for businesses to do tailgating,
  they would have to be in the C-R Zone near the stadium and Forum,
  along with have the additional parking spaces that would be
  designated for the use of tailgating while they are conducting
  regular business. They would be required to obtain Permits and
  Licensing approval and either demonstrate excess Parking
  Available Or provide a Parking Study and request a Special Use
  Permit to allow for the shared overlapping parking usage.

Commissioner Rice asked Ms. Wilcox;
 Please show the C-R Zone that would allow the tailgating parking.
 In getting an understanding, are the Forum and Stadium attempting
  to create a partnership with the community in order to lighten the
  parking load and impact on the stadium and forum is this correct?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the new stadium along with the forum have
  a substantial amount of parking already built-in and available
  for their use.
 If we were to take all of the main arteries into the stadium
  location – La Brea, Prairie, Crenshaw, Florence, Century
  Boulevards, all of those streets that could lighten the impact of
  vehicle parking that would be in the entertainment district, but
  why would the City with no incentives for the property owners, why
  not allow them tailgating to potentially engage with the people
  who would be utilizing their property, especially since they are
  small lots. For a four to six hour holding location for these
  vehicles to come early and do what, since they cannot tailgate,
  to just sit for four to six hours prior to a game looking and
  watching people go by? What would make the property owners want
  to come to City Hall to obtain the permits needed? They could claim
  these people as guest and friends, come and park for four hours,
  and therefore not need to obtain the permits for tailgating. Most
  likely their lot or area would only hold close to 10 to 12
  additional vehicles.

  3
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the amendment allows an expansion of the
  major event parking allowances but tailgating would be limited
  to the C-R zone. This proposal is based on staff research of
  stadium/parking/tailgating operations across the country.

  What is the incentive for the property owners to do this, as
  business owners they would be responsible for the protection of
  those vehicles and no one from the Stadium or Forum are going to
  go over and purchase those 10 to 12 parking spaces and cover those
  vehicles so that they will be protected against any loss and make
  sure things are operating the way that they should. Since that is
  not happening, why not make it possible for those property owners
  to obtain the permits for the 10 to 12 vehicles, if they take good
  care of the people and not charge too much for parking there, most
  likely they will become repeat customers and possibly the property
  owners and the Stadium and Forum can work with the local bus
  companies in the areas to do a circle drive-by of pickups and
  drop-offs of these potential tailgaters, the customers could use
  Uber and Lyft if they didn’t want to walk over to the stadium in
  time for their game, who after spending their time at those
  locations waiting for their particular event to start, maybe even
  stay at the parked area, they can ‘cue and cook at those spaces,
  bring their large screen TV’s and setup and just enjoy the company
  of all who are there.

Chairman Springs stated:
 He feels that the concept/idea of Commissioner Rice is interesting
  and before he allows Commissioner Shaw-Williams an opportunity to
  direct her questions to staff, he feels that Commissioner Rice has
  brought up several good ideas and points that the way this should
  be looked at from other perspectives is such an incentive for the
  local business owners to benefit from the tailgating process and
  as a businessman himself, he too would like to be able to benefit
  from such a possible incentive. He also stated that the possibility
  for the business owners to have potential repeat customers who if
  they find a good parking spot will most likely come back every week
  that there is a game or a concert and these repeat customers might
  want to come every time to that lot due to the benefits of the
  tailgating.
 He also feels that the Planning Commission might want to take
  another look at this and would have to think about the fact that
  the area around the stadium as 9 to 9.5 square miles that would
  be impacted with traffic, how that would affect the community as
  a whole, with the possible gridlock of vehicles in the area.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated currently the code amendment proposes
  expanding the opportunity for businesses to avail themselves
  of the opportunity to provide parking. So this is expanding what
  is currently allowed in the code, geographically. Businesses
  do not have to participate, but the City does have businesses
  that do provide special event parking that was primarily for
  the Forum while they were having performances prior to when
  Covid-19 started, so the City does have businesses who have
  found it financially worthwhile to do this. So based on that,
  staff has expanded the area and it has provided the opportunity
  for more businesses that can provide parking, and the reason
  that staff has omitted the tailgating, is because there are a
  number of Code Enforcement issues potentially associated with
  the tailgating, that will have to be considered. Lastly,
  property owners do have the option of requesting a special
  events permit to offer tailgating events at their sites in
  association with special event parking, so that could be an
  interim approach for allowing for businesses to do the same.

  4
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

  - Ms. Wilcox stated that she is aware that the City is interested
  in getting something in place, since the Stadium is scheduled
  to open up relatively soon

Chairman Springs asked Commissioner  Shaw-Williams  if  she  had
questions for staff or Ms. Wilcox.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated:
 No, Ms. Wilcox has answered all of her questions.

Chairman Springs asked staff for another look at the presentation
map, and stated:
 In the video presentation are various areas around the City that
  show areas where there is excess parking spaces would be businesses
  such as Inglewood Mortuary, Academy Church, 99 Cents Store and Big
  Lots Stores are the only properties that I can see that are on the
  Manchester corridor.
 These stores like the 99 Cents store along with Big Lots are open
  seven days a week, as the Church is mainly open on Sundays, they
  will have to come to the city to ask about utilizing the program?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the 99 Cent’s Store and Big Lots are
  properties that would generally be open during the sports events
  and would have to come to the City and obtain a special event
  parking special use permit and they would have to demonstrate
  that they have the parking available during the events and they
  would have to have at least ten spaces available. Then they could
  apply for the Special Use Permit and go before the Planning
  Commission for their consideration.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated as this is not the C-R zone, they would not
  be able to do tailgating. As currently drafted, tailgating could
  only be conducted in the C-R Zone and at Hollywood Park.
Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Rice if he had anything further
to say or add.
Commissioner Rice stated to staff:
 Special Events Permit is the permit that must be acquired every
  time there is an event that the business would like to hold or host
  for the parking, but the timing of approval is not conducive for
  the business owner, as it will take a full 30 days between each
  approval along with having to go before the Permits and Licensing
  Division which will add more time onto being approved to utilize
  the Special Events Permit, correct?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that is correct.

  He stated that this concerns him very much, that this City cannot
  comply or adhere to what other cities do regarding this particular
  process.

  What we can do is allow the property or business owners to obtain
  the Special Events Permit initially and let them know that if they
  break these specific rules and regulations, their permit will be
  removed, and they cannot function as a Special Events Host any
  longer. Let the business owners and property owners know that they
  will be regulated by Code Enforcement, and if Code Enforcement
  finds that they are not compliant with the rules, they will no
  longer be able to be a Host.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments to speak
for or against this project.

  5
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

FOR / AGAINST
None. This was affirmed by the AT&T On-line Operator.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
final words regarding this particular project.

Commissioner Rice stated:
 That this City is always ahead of other Cities in new and bigger
  ideas and our Planning Staff can be innovative in making this
  particular project a success, this City has done it before and they
  can do it again. Don’t hold everyone accountable for the poor
  activity of one individual business owner, why not let everyone
  in the City profit from this action.

Chairman Springs called for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Patrick to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-040, and adopt a resolution recommending City
Council adoption of Zoning Code Amendment ZCA-2020-001 and was
seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams that Resolution No. 1893;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT ZCA-2020-001 TO AMEND
  CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE (IMC)
  TO MODIFY REGULATIOINS FOR OFF-HOUR PARKING FOR
  MAJOR EVENT PATRONS AND TAILGATING CITYWIDE.

Be approved.

Chairman Springs stated that he had a question on this motion, and
wanted to know if there is a particular way for the Planning
Commission cannot make a motion at this time and have more time to
look at this item again?

Commissioner Patrick stated that there is already a motion on the
floor and it has been seconded.

Chairman Springs asked if there is a way to do a friendly amendment
to the motion?

Commissioner Patrick stated that since she was not certain with doing
the amendment to the motion, as she was unsure of the language for
the amendment, she will withdraw her motion.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated that she will withdraw her second
to the motion.

Assistant Attorney Jeff Lewis, asked Chairman Springs if what the
Planning Commission would like to do is have staff take back this
item and bring it back before the Planning Commission at a later date,
was that what the question is about?

Chairman Springs asked Commissioner Rice to explain the Planning
Commission’s request.

  6
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

Commissioner Rice stated:
 Stated yes, to please bring this back to the Planning Commission
  with having the general public the opportunity to partner with the
  Arena’s and Stadiums by allowing them the same tailgating rights
  but with different restrictions of course.

Assistant City Attorney Jeff Lewis stated that the motion will have
to address whatever restrictions or conditions, requirements that
the zoning code should address or the motion will have to state to
bring it back at a date certain with the points that you consider
some of the things that you are concerned about.
He stated or the Planning Commission will have to address it now and
put in the language now if you want to pass this item this evening.
Chairman Springs called for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Patrick to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-040, and adopt a resolution recommending City
Council adoption of Zoning Code Amendment ZCA-2020-001 and
Commissioner Rice asked for a Friendly Amendment to the motion prior
to giving his second to the motion, by asking the planning staff to
work on the Zoning Code with reference to the Tailgating
restrictions, that creates some Code enforcement rules that will
apply to the people who want to partner with the City and in the
creation to a new department and was seconded by Commissioner Rice
that Resolution No. 1893;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT ZCA-2020-001 TO AMEND
  CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE (IMC)
  TO MODIFY REGULATIOINS FOR OFF-HOUR PARKING FOR
  MAJOR EVENT PATRONS AND TAILGATING CITYWIDE.

Be approved.

Assistant Attorney Lewis stated that he wanted to ensure that the
Planning Division is clear and fully understands what the Planning
Commission wants and needs staff to do with regards to this Zoning
Code Amendment?
Then Assistant Attorney Lewis asked Commissioner Rice  if  he
understands exactly what he needs to do in his motion?

Commissioner Rice asked:
 Does the motion have to be re-stated?
 Well, what I’m trying to say is that there needs to be a partnership
  between the community and the stadiums and arenas.
 That there needs to be rules for property owners and commercial
  businesses holding/hosting tailgating/parking areas/facilities
  throughout the City and they should have the same rules as what
  the Arenas and Stadiums have regarding tailgating. No different
  set of rules for one group over another regarding tailgating.

Assistant City Attorney Lewis stated that he also feels that is
important that staff knows exactly what the planning commission would
like.

  7
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

Ms. Wilcox stated that staff is understanding what the planning
commission is requesting, and with that, can still take it before
the City Council, with the understanding that staff has not fully
evaluated all consequences and situations that may occur as a result
of these revised tailgating provisions to allow it throughout the
City at the various parking sites. So either staff can bring it back
to the Planning Commission or can take it forward to the City Council
as is.
Chairman Springs suggested and requested:
 Planning Staff bring the item back before the Planning Commission
  after modifications.

Commissioner Patrick asked:
 Should the planning commission make the return date specific or
  should staff put it off for the next 60 days?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that if they chose date specific, this item
  can be moved to the next March 3, 2021 Planning Commission
  meeting.
Commissioner Rice asked to make one more statement:
 This will be in the best interest of the City if this is laid-out
  properly.

Assistant City Attorney Lewis stated that if what is desired is for
the Planning Staff to bring this item back before the planning
commission within 30 days, possibly it would be best for the motion
to be stated as a continuance with the recommendations from the
planning commission rather than a motion to affirm or approve the
project.

Chairman Springs stated
 He agrees.

Commissioner Patrick stated:
 She withdrew her motion.
 March 3, 2021 the planning commission will re-address this issue
  after the recommendations are considered.
 Planning Commission will discuss it further at the March 3, 2021
  Planning Commission Meeting.

Chairman Springs stated:
 Correct.

Commissioner Patrick made the new motion to continue Item 5b, Zoning
Code Amendment 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001) until the March 3, 2021
Planning Commission Meeting and to be discussed further
incorporating the recommendations of the planning commission and was
seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs

Chairman Springs stated:
 He feels that with the incorporation of the suggestions of
  Commissioner Rice that a partnership for the community with the
  City would be for the best for not only the city, but also for the
  community at large, property owners and business owners.

  8
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 3, 2021

(6) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None
The AT&T Operator opened the lines of communication to the public
